# SK0216 — The argument naming style is not arranged

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

`skala arrange` would add or remove argument names under the configured style.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Formatting |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | no |
| Language version floor | — |
| Since | 2.0 |

## Why

Adding a name requires the resolved parameter; removing one is safe only when the argument already occupies that parameter's position. The rule binds the selected overload and preserves names that carry ordering semantics, and it binds the rewritten call against the whole method group: a name is added or removed only where overload resolution still selects the same member, so a name that picks the overload, or would pick another one, stays as written.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
Move(x: 1, y: 2);
```

Write:

```csharp
Move(1, 2);
```

## When it does not fire

Unresolved calls, out-of-position arguments, expanded `params` arguments that cannot legally be named, and names overload resolution depends on are left alone.

## Configuration

- `skala_arguments_literal`
- `skala_arguments_string_literal`
- `skala_arguments_anonymous_function`
- `skala_arguments_named`
- `skala_arguments_other`
- `skala_arguments_skip_single`
